note:
DEPTH PASS (the base console is merged). Goal: turn this service's sub-sections and config sections into REAL backend integrations. For EACH capability entry listed in `depth_targets` decide:

  KEEP HONEST — only if it needs something a local simulator cannot run (a separate product, real hardware/network, billing, third-party identity): leave it NotSimulated and put the concrete reason in the entry's `limitations`.
Prefer behaviour that is ENFORCED (e.g. lifecycle rules actually expire objects, a DLQ really receives, a policy really denies) over config that is only stored. Real coverage must go UP; nothing may regress: fidelity ≥ 90%, every capability claim true on nano AND offline, smokes green. Do not edit consoles/honest-allowlist.json or .github/.
House rules: keep consoles/src/<cloud>/kit/Capability.jsx as on base (add JSON imports only), list the service ONCE in registry.js, register any NEW core in wasm/build_cores.py + wasm/nano-boot.js (own line, never inside a // comment) + core/nano_registry.py + core/nano_persist.py (tests/conformance/test_nano_core_manifest.py), unique variable names in the smoke files, 'Vyomi' as plain text, re-vendor with python3 wasm/build_cores.py, rebuild bundles, COMMIT your source.

Run the gate, the cloud's smoke, and the conformance tests in the FOREGROUND before your final message; commit source.

depth_targets.title: Detailed monitoring flag
limitations: Enabling detailed monitoring is stored and returned from DescribeInstances, but Vyomi has no CloudWatch metrics pipeline for EC2 — no CPU/network data points are actually collected.

depth_targets.title: CloudWatch alarms and instance metrics
limitations: CloudWatch alarms for an instance aren't modeled; there is no alarm evaluation backend.

No CloudWatch metrics are collected: CPU utilization (%), Network in (bytes), Network out (bytes), Network packets in (count), Network packets out (count), Status check failed (any) (count), CPU credit usage (count), CPU credit balance (count).

depth_targets.title: Connect (SSH / RDP / EC2 Instance Connect / Session Manager)
limitations: Vyomi instances aren't real virtual machines with a reachable network stack, so there is nothing to SSH, RDP or Session-Manager into.

depth_targets.title: AMI catalog — AWS Marketplace AMIs / Community AMIs
limitations: Vyomi has no connection to AWS Marketplace or the community AMI catalog; only AMIs you've created or the built-in quickstart set are available.

depth_targets.title: Amazon Data Lifecycle Manager (automated snapshot/AMI policies)
limitations: Scheduled lifecycle policies aren't modeled; create snapshots and AMIs directly instead.

depth_targets.title: Security group sharing (AWS RAM) and VPC associations
limitations: Cross-account sharing via AWS Resource Access Manager isn't modeled; every security group stays scoped to this account and its one default VPC.

depth_targets.title: Placement groups
limitations: Partition groups assign and round-robin a real partition number, and spread groups enforce AWS's 7-running-instances-per-Availability-Zone cap, but there are no real racks or hosts underneath — cluster placement has no network-latency effect and a spread group's instances aren't actually host-isolated.

depth_targets.title: Key pairs (create, import, delete)
limitations: CreateKeyPair returns a private-key-shaped document and a fingerprint derived from it, but it is not real RSA/ED25519 key material — it cannot be used to open a real SSH session (see ec2.instances.connect).

depth_targets.title: Allowed AMIs, Managed resources, EC2 Serial Console, Auto Scaling group defaults, Zones
limitations: These account-wide EC2 settings aren't modeled; they have no effect in Vyomi.

depth_targets.title: Load balancers, target groups, trust stores
limitations: Elastic Load Balancing isn't part of the EC2 console surface Vyomi simulates.

depth_targets.title: Auto Scaling groups
limitations: Auto Scaling isn't modeled; launch and manage instances directly.

depth_targets.title: Spot Requests, Savings Plans, Reserved Instances, Dedicated Hosts, Capacity Reservations, UltraServers, Capacity Manager
limitations: Vyomi has one simple on-demand pricing/availability model; these purchasing and capacity-planning products aren't simulated.
